result: {"decisions":[{"point":"D1","problem":"How to evaluate whether activation verbalizers generalize to practically relevant tasks far from their training distribution, and compare against other methods.","did":"They evaluated AOs on downstream auditing tasks (secret-keeping, emergent misalignment) where activations come from fine-tuned models never seen in training and prior white- and black-box baselines exist.","alternatives_named":["narrow evaluations such as held-out SAE features or user attributes"],"stated_reason":"Prior evaluations were narrow and did not study generalization to very different tasks where LatentQA decoders could be compared to baseline methods.","quote":"Notably, these downstream tasks permit comparison to other methods, allowing us to put the performance of AOs in context."},{"point":"D2","problem":"How to apply the AO to the emergent misalignment audit so it reflects what fine-tuning changed rather than the prompt content.","did":"They fed the AO the difference between base and fine-tuned model activations and plugged it into the existing agentic auditing scaffold in place of ADL, using one fixed open-ended prompt with no per-task tuning.","alternatives_named":["ADL with PatchScopes and activation steering requiring per-task tuning","multi-turn interactions"],"stated_reason":"Using a single fixed prompt demonstrates the AO needs no per-task tuning, and multi-turn interactions did not improve the agent's score.","quote":"We replace ADL with our Activation Oracle, which interprets the same activation difference vectors despite never being trained on them. This requires no per-task tuning, as we simply provide the difference vectors and a fixed open-ended oracle prompt"},{"point":"D5","problem":"How to interpret the AO's 2/5 score on emergent misalignment models given a rubric designed for generally misaligned models.","did":"They argued that 2/5 is near the achievable maximum because the models, trained with chat data, showed almost no emergent misalignment, so higher rubric scores were effectively unattainable.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"Scores of 3/5 and above require identifying misaligned behaviors that the models do not display.","quote":"Because these models exhibit minimal emergent misalignment, the maximum achievable audit score is effectively 2/5. Scores of 3/5 and above require the auditor to identify specific misaligned behaviors, which is not possible when the models do not display such behaviors."},{"point":"D2","problem":"Which activation tokens to supply as AO input for secret-keeping evaluations, given that token selection affects performance.","did":"They used the full sequence of activations as the default for all secret-keeping evaluations while reporting that single-token or short selections can do better on some tasks.","alternatives_named":["single-token inputs on Taboo","shorter selected sequences for Gender"],"stated_reason":"Simplicity and consistency, and in real auditing without ground-truth labels it is hard to sweep token selection as a hyperparameter.","quote":"For all secret-keeping evaluations, we use the full sequence of activations as input for simplicity and consistency, though we find that alternative token selections can improve performance, such as single-token inputs on the Taboo task and shorter selected sequences for Gender"},{"point":"D1","problem":"Whether gains from the full training mixture come from data diversity or merely from more examples.","did":"They ran a controlled ablation on Qwen3-8B comparing an SPQA+Classification baseline and a truncated full mixture, both at 400k examples, plus the full 1M mixture.","alternatives_named":["scaling the mixture only, which confounds diversity and quantity"],"stated_reason":"Adding datasets increases both example count and diversity, so holding sample count fixed separates the effects.","quote":"Adding datasets increases both the number of examples and the diversity of training signals. To tease apart these effects, we run a controlled ablation on Qwen3-8B that focuses on the impact of adding our self-supervised context prediction task"},{"point":"D5","problem":"How to interpret the low absolute PersonaQA accuracy of open-source AOs (about 14%) when the achievable ceiling is unknown.","did":"They contextualized the result by noting the unclear skyline, a linear probe baseline of only 25% on a related dataset, and brittle fine-tuned knowledge, while still concluding AOs extract some signal.","alternatives_named":["training a linear probe baseline"],"stated_reason":"The PersonaQA-shuffled dataset has too few instances per attribute to train probes, and models drop to near-chance on yes/no reformulations.","quote":"The skyline for this task is unclear: the PersonaQA-shuffled dataset we use lacks sufficient attributes to train a linear probe baseline (often just 3-5 instances of a given attribute exist), and in a related dataset where linear probes were feasible, Li et al. (2025b) found they achieved only 25% accuracy."},{"point":"D4","problem":"Whether to continue the hallucination detection line of work after a preliminary experiment.","did":"They dropped hallucination detection as a primary evaluation after an anecdotal test showed a simple black-box follow-up-question baseline performed similarly.","alternatives_named":["pursuing hallucination detection as a primary evaluation task"],"stated_reason":"The setting did not show a clear advantage for activation-based methods over prompting, and the experiment was highly anecdotal.","quote":"Because this setting did not appear to offer a clear advantage for activation-based methods over straightforward prompting, and because our experiment was highly anecdotal, we did not pursue hallucination detection as a primary evaluation task in this work."},{"point":"D4","problem":"Whether to include SAE feature interpretation datasets in the AO training mixture.","did":"They training"],"stated_reason":"Limited downstream benefits, added implementation complexity, and nontrivial compute and API cost.","quote":"Given the limited downstream benefits, the additional results."},{"point":"D6","problem":"How strongly to state the claim that diverse training improves AOs given that gains vary across models and tasks.","did":"They claimed consistent improvement from tasks.","alternatives_named":[],"stated_reason":"On Gemma/Llama secret-keeping SPQA-only is within error of white-box baselines, whereas on Qwen3-8B tasks scaling yields much larger improvements.","quote":"In contrast, on Qwen3-8B evaluations such as PersonaQA and Taboo (Figure 19), scaling the training mixture yields much larger improvements, indicating that the value of added
